• It is separated from the Asian mainland by the Sea of Japan, and from India by the Indian Ocean and several Southeast Asian countries.

questions.question: India has an open border with which of the following countries?
questions.solution:

__
 
• India shares an **open border** with **Nepal**.
 
• This means that the movement of people between the two countries is largely unrestricted.
 
• The open border facilitates trade, commerce, and cultural exchange between India and Nepal.
 
• **Citizens of both countries can travel without the need for a visa or passport**, adhering to certain identification requirements.
 
• The open border agreement is a significant aspect of the friendly and cooperative relationship between India and Nepal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The India-Nepal open border is established under the **1950 Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship**.
 
• The treaty allows for free movement of people and goods between the two nations and grants reciprocal rights of residence, ownership of property, participation in trade and commerce, and other privileges.
 
• This open border has historical significance and has been in place for decades, reflecting the deep-rooted ties between the two countries.
 
• Despite the open border, both nations have established mechanisms to address security concerns and manage cross-border activities effectively.
 
• The open border is a unique feature of India-Nepal relations and is not common with India's other neighboring countries.

• In 1982, the area was closed to climbers and trekkers to preserve its natural environment, although some parts have since been reopened under strict regulations.
 
• The peak is named after the Hindu goddess Nanda Devi, who is revered as the patron deity of the region.
 
• Efforts are continuously made to balance ecological preservation with sustainable tourism in the area.

questions.question: Which physical feature of India prevents the cold winds from central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinents?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Himalayas**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayas are the physical feature that prevents cold winds from Central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinent**
 
• The **Himalayas are a lofty mountain range that blocks cold winds from Central Asia from entering India.**
 
• The Himalayas' height, location, and complex topography significantly impact the climate of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The **Himalayas also influence the monsoons, forcing the rain-bearing winds to lose most of their moisture before crossing the range. **
 
• The Himalayas cause the Indian subcontinent to experience milder winters than Central Asia.
 
• **Northern India also has higher temperatures than other areas on the same latitudes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian plain**s

 
 
• **The Northern Plains, also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plain**, are the granaries of India and the foundation for early civilizations.
 
• This vast plain is formed by the **rivers Ganga**, **Yamuna**, **Brahmaputra**, and their tributaries.
 
• It stretches across northern and northeastern India, covering states like **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, **West Bengal**, **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• The Indo-Gangetic plain is characterized by fertile soils, making it one of the most important agricultural regions in India.
 
• It is densely populated, with major cities like **Delhi**, **Kolkata**, **Lucknow**, and **Patna** located along its course.
 
 
 
• **Indian desert**
 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is India's largest desert, covering about 77,000 square miles.
 
• The Thar Desert spans across parts of **Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, **Punjab**, and **Haryana** in India, extending into **Pakistan**.
 
• It covers around **200,000 square kilometres** in India, primarily in the state of Rajasthan.
 
• The desert supports sparse vegetation like **cactus**, **acacia trees**, and **scrub plants**.
 
 
 
• **Coastal area**s
 
 
• **India's coastal areas include the coastal states of Gujarat**, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal, as well as the coastal union territories of Daman & Diu, Puducherry, Lakshadweep Islands, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
 
• **Coastal plains are low-lying**, flat areas of land that are adjacent to the sea or ocean.
 
• The elevation of the land increases gradually from the sea to the highlands. 
 
• **India's other main physical features include the Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the characteristic features of the Indian Desert?

options.text: It is also known as Marusthali.
It lies northwest of the Aravalli hills.
It receives 250 mm rainfall per year.

questions.solution:
The current answer is __**It receives 250 mm rainfall per year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The defining characteristics of the** Indian Desert** include its vast expanse of **sand dunes and an annual rainfall of less than 150 mm**. 
 
• Situated between the** Aravalli Mountains** and the plains formed by the **Sutlej and Indus rivers**, it's also known as the **Thar Desert**. 
 
• Comprised mainly of rocks and sand, it exhibits a harsh, dry climate, with temperatures ranging from near freezing to a** scorching 50°C**. 
 
• Despite the challenging conditions, some areas experience a fleeting spring season. 
 
• This region, although densely populated, presents a formidable environment for human, plant, and animal survival compared to other landscapes. 
 
• Millet stands out as the primary crop cultivated in the Indian Desert.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Thar Desert, **also referred to as the** Great Indian Desert,** sprawls across the north-western region of the Indian subcontinent, spanning approximately 200,000 km² (77,000 sq mi) across India and Pakistan.
 
• Ranking as the **18th largest desert **globally and the 9th largest hot subtropical desert, it boasts an arid and subtropical climate.
 
• Temperature fluctuations are notable between seasons, ranging from near-freezing in winter to over 50°C during the summer months.
 
• Annual rainfall averages between 100 to 500 mm, primarily occurring in the brief July-to-September southwest monsoon period.
 
• The desert comprises a distinctly dry area, Marusthali, in the west, contrasted by a semidesert section in the east, characterized by fewer sand dunes and slightly increased precipitation.

questions.question: The Deccan Plateau is a _________landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.

• The plateau is also home to several major rivers, including the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri, which are vital for irrigation and water supply in the region.

questions.question: The northern plain of the Indian subcontinent has been formed by the interplay of the three major river systems along with their tributaries. Choose the odd one out of the options given.

__
 
• The Godavari is one of the longest rivers in India but it does not contribute to the formation of the northern plains.
 
• The northern plains of India are primarily formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra river systems.
 
• The Godavari river primarily flows through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha, contributing to the Deccan Plateau region.
 
• The Godavari is often referred to as the 'Dakshina Ganga' or 'Ganga of the South' due to its large size and significance in southern India.

• It is known for creating significant alluvial deposits in the Assam Valley, contributing to the formation of the northern plains.
 
 
 
• **The Indus**
 
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, originating in Tibet and flowing through India and Pakistan.
 
• It plays a crucial role in forming the fertile plains of Punjab and Sindh, which are part of the northern plains.
 
 
 
• **The Ganga**
 
 
• The Ganga is the most significant river of northern India, originating from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas.
 
• It contributes heavily to the alluvial deposits that form the vast fertile plains of North India, known as the Gangetic plains.
 
 
 
• **Formation of the Northern Plains**
 
 
• The northern plains are formed by the sediment deposits of the three major river systems: the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra.
 
• These plains are characterized by fertile alluvial soil, making them one of the most agriculturally productive regions in the world.
 
• The plains extend across several states in India, including Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam.
